evidence: Vitr. 8.5.2: sī aequāliter aqua canālis summa labra tanget, sciētur esse lībrātum
terms.comment: Levelled, as with the lībra or lībella, the builder’s level (see “level (instrument)”): Vitruvius’s word for what is truly horizontal, as the surface of still water is.

evidence: Varr. RR 1.6: quam is quī est ad lībellam aequos
terms.comment: “By the level”: the builders’ and farmers’ phrase, as ad perpendiculum is for upright (see “vertical”). So also ad lībram (Caes. B.C. 3.40: ad lībram fēcerat turrēs).
Of a line or a bar that lies across another, as a crossbar across uprights (see “crossbar”). In drawing it is the natural word for a line that runs across.

phrases.latin: Līneam lībrātam ā sinistrā ad dextram dūc, quālis est summa aqua in pōculō.
phrases.english: Draw a level line from left to right, like the top of the water in a cup.

phrases.latin: et sī aequāliter aqua canālis summa labra tanget, sciētur esse lībrātum
phrases.english: and if the water touches the top edges of the channel evenly, you will know it is level

phrases.latin: Campester locus is melior, quī tōtus aequābiliter in ūnam partem verget, quam is quī est ad lībellam aequos
phrases.english: Flat land is better if it all slopes evenly one way than if it is dead level

sources: Lewis & Short: libro · Lewis & Short: libella · Lewis & Short: transverto
